name: Kappa Tower III
award: 2024 Federal 9% and state housing tax credits (Round One)
headline: Kappa Housing Inc., a nonprofit founded by members of the Kappa Alpha Psi fraternity, built Kappa Tower III, a 30-unit building for seniors 62 and older at 30% to 50% AMI next to its Kappa Tower II in Denver's Central Park neighborhood, with a 2024 Round One 9% and state credit award from CHFA.
why_it_matters: It shows how a small nonprofit used its own already-improved land and a second-phase site next to an existing building to win a 9% award for a 30-unit deeply affordable senior project, after losing in 2023, and reached a grand opening about two years after the award.

status.label: Grand opening held 2026-07-16, per the architect; lease-up not confirmed
status.detail: Front Porch reported a groundbreaking in late September 2025. Denver announced City Council approval of a $1,050,000 loan on 2026-06-17. The architect, KEPHART, posted on 2026-07-24 that the grand opening was held on July 16 (the year 2026 is inferred from the post date). No public record of a certificate of occupancy or occupancy level was found.

next_step: Watch for a CHFA placed-in-service record or 8609 and a property listing showing occupancy at the 9095 E. 48th Ave. address.

background.text: Kappa Tower III is the second phase on the Kappa Tower II site. Kappa Tower II, a 70-unit senior building for 30% to 60% AMI, was completed in 2021; Denver says it was the first age- and income-restricted housing added to the Central Park area since 2003.

The project applied in 2023 and did not win: CHFA's 2023 Round One letter-of-intent report lists Kappa Tower III (30 units) with a $1,300,000 request. The 2024 narrative says the plans had not changed and that the contractor kept cost increases small.
The award was smaller than the request: $941,084 against $1,168,378 requested in the 2024 applicant report.

Readiness as stated in the application: use-by-right zoning, a pre-application meeting held with the city, about six months of construction documents and seven months of permitting, and construction start in the second quarter of 2025. Front Porch reported the groundbreaking in late September 2025.

The market study in the application gave a capture rate of 23.4% for existing projects, rising to 25.3% with these 30 units, and forecast lease-up within two months. The environmental report found no concerns.

Accessibility: the applicant planned ADA-accessible tubs in this phase at residents' request, and Denver says the units include features for residents with disabilities who need help with daily living.

discrepancies.text: CHFA's award and applicant reports give the address as 9063 Northfield Boulevard, the application narrative and CHFA's 2023 letter-of-intent report give 9020 Northfield Blvd. (Kappa Tower II's address), and Denver's loan announcement gives 9095 East 48th Avenue.
KEPHART describes Kappa Tower III as serving seniors at 30% to 60% AMI, while CHFA's award description and Denver's loan announcement put all units at 30% to 50% AMI.

The application narrative says the land is donated by Forest City, while CHFA's award description says the sponsor is providing the land at no cost and Denver says the building uses part of the Kappa Tower II site.
